Clarke Lane Job Board. This short video follows one order, from the sales order to the invoice. Everything you see is practice data.
On changeover day, open the Xero tab and press Import open sales orders, once. Every open sales order in Xero is brought onto Won quotes.
Won quotes lists the orders brought in from Xero, and any quote Levi marks as ordered in the quote calculator. Press Create sales order on one.
The order form fills itself in: the customer, the lines, the prices and the due dates. Check the customer's P O, and tick the processes the job needs.
Press Create sales order. It gets the next S O number, and the order acknowledgement is ready to email to the customer.
Open the order from Sales orders to see everything about it: the lines, drawings, processes, dispatches, purchase orders and pro formas.

Drop P D F drawings onto the order, or press Attach. They're saved in SharePoint and open full screen on the shop floor. The board also reads the drawing, the material, the folds, tapped holes and powder coat, and suggests any process the order is missing. Add them, or press Not needed.

Buying in parts, or outside work like painting? Press New purchase order. To repeat one, pick it under Copy a previous P O, and the supplier, account and lines fill in. Or pick the supplier from Xero, and the account: materials are five thousand. For an order you buy in and send on, tick Back-to-back on the sales order, and its P O opens ready with the same parts. It goes to Xero as a draft P O, with the S O number on it.
If the customer needs to pay first, press New pro forma. Email it, and Keith is copied in automatically. The customer pays quoting the P F number. Press Mark paid when the money arrives.
Print the job sheet for the job folder. It shows what to make and the processes to tick, with no prices.
On Sales orders, tick the orders you want, and the bar at the bottom adds up their value. Press Clear when you're done.

Parts, from Sales orders, keeps each customer's part numbers with their drawings. Add a part, attach its drawing once, and it attaches itself to every new order for that part. Part numbers already on orders are suggested, ready to add.

Jobs lists every open job, soonest due first. Click a due date to change it, or drag a job to bring it forward. The shop floor follows this order. For Levi, one line at the top shows the month so far. The full picture is on Home.
This is the shop floor screen. Tap your station to see the jobs waiting there, in the order to do them.

When a process is finished, tap its step, and it turns green. Press Drawing to see the drawing full screen. Tap a green step again to undo it. Levi and Mandy can also change the order at one station, with the arrows on each job. Only that station changes.

Powder coat and plating are done by another company. At the P coat station, press Send out, and put in the company, what's going, the colour, and when it's due back. The Sent out tile is the whiteboard: every job at each company, with anything overdue in red. When it comes back, press Back in, and the process is ticked done.
When every process is ticked, the job shows Ready to dispatch, and it appears on the Dispatch tab.

On Dispatch, choose what's going, all of it or part, and press Create dispatch note. Then email it to the customer, print it, or press Save P D F. The file is named with the customer, the note number and the order, ready to keep.
Once it's delivered, the note waits under Waiting for Xero. Tick it and press Send to Xero. That makes one draft invoice for exactly what was sent, ready for Keith to approve.

For Levi and Mandy, Home also shows customers with invoices over sixty days, and past due in Xero. Press Draft a chase email, and a polite reminder, with each invoice and a link to pay online, lands in Outlook Drafts, copied to Keith. And when a new order is for one of these customers, the order form warns you.

And every morning, start on Home. It shows what's late, what's due this week, what's ready to go, and the invoicing to do. For Levi, it shows the month too: invoiced, including anything raised in Xero outside the board, work in progress, and the gap to target. That's the whole process.
